newsitem.title: USA: Troy, N.Y. to give city panel refinancing plan Wed.
newsitem.headline: Troy, N.Y. to give city panel refinancing plan Wed.

text.p: Troy, N.Y., whose bondholders at the last minute agreed to waive a lease payment the city looked likely to default on, said it plans to present its refinancing plan to the finance committee on Wednesday.
The city panel is expected to take about one week to analyze the plan, which then will be voted on by the nine-member city council, said Owen Goldfarb, Troy's budget director.
While the council recently held up part of the refinancing before finally approving the plan, Goldfarb said officials were cautiously optimistic that the new restructuring pact will be enacted.
Mayor Mark Pattison has said the refinancing would save the city $11 million and cut its debt service so that it does not exceed $6 million a year.

Troy, which has a population of about 55,000 people, in July had around $90 million of long-term obligations. The debt includes about $35 million of leaseback debt that was issued in 1992, which paid 8.8 percent interest due to the deal's unusual structure.

Three bondholders were owed a $1.4 million lease revenue payment on the $35 million of debt, but the city has said it did not have enough money in its reserve account to make the payment, which was due on September 15.
